subject: Acme Health renewal & capacity commit — pricing and credits
messages:
From: Sarah Bell <sarah.bell@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal quote and capacity increase — Acme Health

Marissa,

Renewal for our Redwood contract is up on 2026-04-01. Our usage is trending up and we expect to need roughly 2x our committed capacity over the next 12 months. Procurement asked me to start pricing now — specifically:

- Pricing options for a 12-month and 24-month renewal with a capacity increase of ~2x
- Any available multi-year discounts or credits for committing early
- Possibility of a temporary price hold for the next 6 months while we finish a large purchase order

Can you share a preliminary proposal? I can loop in procurement for contract redline once we have numbers.

Thanks,
Sarah Bell
Director of Platform
Acme Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 21 Feb 2026 10:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal quote and capacity increase — Acme Health

Hi Sarah — thanks for the heads up and the usage snapshot. Short version: we can get you competitive economics either with a larger committed spend or a multi-year deal. Two options to consider (high level):

1) One-year renewal + capacity commit (2x): 10% renewal credit applied to next invoice OR one-time $30k account credit; price per token remains the same. Requires signed amendment by 2026-03-15.

2) Two-year renewal: 8–12% discount on list with a 24‑month commit; we can offer a 6-month price hold on the first year if you sign by 2026-03-15.

We can also do a short-term price hold (3–6 months) while you finalize procurement paperwork, but that usually requires a firm commit to increase capacity after the hold. I attached a preliminary pricing workbook to show the delta against your current commit.

Proposed next step: 30-min call early next week to confirm target commit and finalize which structure you prefer. Is Tue 2/24 at 10am PT possible?

Attachments: Redwood_prelim_pricing_acme.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Renewal quote and capacity increase — Acme Health (approval request)

Vivek / Aditya — looping you both in. Acme (Sarah Bell) needs pricing for a renewal with ~2x capacity increase. They are open to 1yr or 2yr. From my ask:

- If we do a 1yr with 2x commit, I suggested a one-time $30k credit OR a 10% renewal credit.
- For a 2yr we can offer 8–12% off list and a 6-month price hold on year 1.

Their procurement team often pushes for a price hold + a smaller discount; I think offering a credit is cleaner for accounting. Asking for signoff to present a best-case commercial: $45k one-time credit + 12% off first-year list if they sign a 12-month expanded commit by 2026-03-15. That would close the expansion and keep unit economics fair.

Can you confirm whether $45k credit + 12% on year-1 is permissible, or if we should stick to $30k / 10%? Also want to confirm if Legal needs any special terms for the price hold option.

Thanks — I can present either option on the call.

Warmly,
Marissa

Marissa — I reviewed the account and the forecast. High level: we should be aggressive to secure the commit and expansion. Approve the following commercial trap: 

- Offer a one-time $45,000 credit against their next invoice if they sign a 12‑month expanded commit (2x capacity) by 2026-03-15.
- In addition, provide 12% off first-year list pricing (applies to the committed capacity only).
- For customers requesting a price hold: allow a 6-month hold with the same above economics if they sign an LOI and show a PO within 30 days of the hold expiration.

Do not make the credit refundable and require standard termination language. Legal should review the LOI/Amendment; I cc'ed Aditya to start the paperwork prep.

Vivek Kulkarni

Marissa — thanks for circling back and for the detailed options. We discussed internally and procurement asked for the following counter: 

- We accept the one-time $45,000 credit applied to the next invoice.
- We need a 6-month price hold starting from 2026-04-01 through 2026-09-30. During the hold, we request a 15% discount on committed capacity for the first 3 months of the hold (as a ramp incentive), then revert to the 12% you offered for the remainder of year 1.
- We will sign a 12-month expanded commit (2x) if you can confirm the hold + ramp discount in an LOI by 2026-03-10. Procurement also asked for Net 45 payment terms on the first invoice reflecting the credit.

If you can send an LOI/Amendment with those points and a DocuSign link, we'll route for procurement approval.

Appreciate the flexibility — Sarah
Sarah Bell
